lightClock.takeaway: Both photons travel at c. The moving one simply has farther to go, so its clock ticks slower by γ.

spacetime.orderAgreed: Every frame agrees on this order.
spacetime.orderDisputed: Change β and the order flips — neither event causes the other.

twinParadox.takeaway: The turn is what breaks the symmetry: at that instant the traveller's "now" on Earth jumps forward.
twinParadox.dragHint: Drag the turn event to change the trip.

relativisticDoppler.takeaway: Even straight across, with nothing approaching or receding, the light is redshifted by γ.

screenSummary.playArea: The play area shows two identical light clocks. The upper one is at rest in the laboratory; the lower one glides past at an adjustable fraction of the speed of light, its photon tracing a zigzag.
screenSummary.controlArea: The control area has a relative velocity slider, a mirror separation slider, photon path and light-travel triangle checkboxes, time controls, and a Reset All button that returns the simulation to its starting state.
screenSummary.interactionHint: Change the relative velocity and watch the two tick counts drift apart, then change the mirror separation and watch their ratio stay put.

lightClock.currentDetails: At a relative velocity of {{beta}} times the speed of light, gamma is {{gamma}}. The lab clock has counted {{restTicks}} ticks and the moving clock {{movingTicks}}.

controls.velocityHelp: Speed of the moving light clock, as a fraction of the speed of light.
controls.showTrailHelp: Show the zigzag the moving photon traces through the laboratory.
controls.mirrorSeparationHelp: Distance between the mirrors of both clocks, in light-seconds. One tick takes twice this long.
controls.showTriangleHelp: Show the right triangle whose legs are how far the clock moved and how far the photon crossed, and whose hypotenuse is how far the photon flew.

screenSummary.playArea: The play area shows a spacetime diagram with space across and time up. Two draggable events, A and B, sit on it, along with the light cone through the origin and the axes of a second frame moving at an adjustable velocity.
screenSummary.controlArea: The control area has a relative velocity slider, checkboxes for the light cone, the moving frame, lines of simultaneity, invariant hyperbolas and coordinate projections, buttons that boost to event B's frame and to the frame where the events are simultaneous, and a Reset All button.
screenSummary.interactionHint: Drag an event outside the light cone, then sweep the velocity and watch which event comes first change.

spacetime.currentDetails: Event A is at x {{ax}}, ct {{act}} light-seconds; event B is at x {{bx}}, ct {{bct}}. Their separation is {{separation}} with interval squared {{interval}}. At a relative velocity of {{beta}} times the speed of light, {{order}}.

controls.velocityHelp: Speed of the second frame, as a fraction of the speed of light. Its axes shear towards the light cone as this grows.
controls.eventAHelp: Drag to move event A through space and time.
controls.eventBHelp: Drag to move event B through space and time.
controls.boostToBHelp: Slide the relative velocity to the value that puts event B at rest, if one exists.
controls.boostToSimultaneity: Boost to the frame where A and B are simultaneous
controls.boostToSimultaneityHelp: Slide the relative velocity to the value that makes the two events happen at the same time, if one exists.

screenSummary.playArea: The play area shows a spacetime diagram carrying two worldlines from the same start to the same finish: the stay-at-home twin's straight vertical line, and the travelling twin's out-and-back path through a draggable turn event.
screenSummary.controlArea: The control area has a journey scrubber measured in Earth seconds, traveller's now and light signals checkboxes, journey time controls, and a Reset All button that returns the simulation to its starting state.
screenSummary.interactionHint: Drag the turn event, then play the journey and compare the two clocks — or turn on the light signals and count the flashes instead.

twinParadox.currentDetails: The turn is at x {{x}}, ct {{ct}} light-seconds, an outbound speed of {{beta}} times the speed of light with gamma {{gamma}}. At the reunion the Earth clock reads {{earth}} seconds and the traveller's clock {{traveller}}.

controls.turnaroundHelp: Drag to change how far and how fast the travelling twin goes.
controls.showSimultaneityHelp: Show which moment on Earth the traveller currently calls now.
controls.journeyHelp: Scrub through the trip. Measured in seconds on the Earth clock, and stops at the reunion.
controls.showSignalsHelp: Show the light pulses each twin sends the other once per second of their own time.

screenSummary.playArea: The play area shows a light source sweeping past a draggable observer, emitting expanding wavefronts. The colour the observer receives shifts from blue to red as the source passes, and a lobe shows how the source's brightness is beamed forward.
screenSummary.controlArea: The control area has a source velocity slider, an emitted wavelength slider, wavefront, beaming and light ray checkboxes, time controls, and a Reset All button.
screenSummary.interactionHint: Set a high source velocity and watch the received colour swing through the spectrum as the source goes by, then drag the observer and watch the swing change shape.

relativisticDoppler.currentDetails: The source moves at {{beta}} times the speed of light, emitting {{emitted}} nanometres. The observer receives {{observed}} nanometres, a Doppler factor of {{doppler}} and a relative brightness of {{brightness}}.

controls.velocityHelp: Speed of the light source, as a fraction of the speed of light.
controls.wavelengthHelp: Wavelength the source emits in its own rest frame, in nanometres.
controls.observerHelp: Drag to change where the observer stands, and so the angle the light arrives at.
controls.showLightRayHelp: Show where the source was when it emitted the light arriving now, and the path that light took.

preferences.title: Simulation
preferences.showRapidityDescription: Add the rapidity η = artanh β beside the γ readout. Rapidity adds when boosts are combined, where β does not.
preferences.shadeLightConeDescription: Start the Spacetime Diagram and Twin Paradox screens with the causal future and past already shaded.
